chunks: From him, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the traveler going to Mecca and other places, is he obligated to perform the prayer of the two Eids, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha? He said: 'Yes, except in Mina on the Day of Sacrifice.'
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: Its meaning is that it is recommended for him, based on the indication of the narrations we presented earlier, and this is confirmed by what he narrated:

key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْعِيدَيْنِ: The prayer of the two Eids

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Eid prayers for a traveler in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Rida (AS), clarifying that while Eid prayers are generally obligatory or highly recommended for travelers, the specific exemption applies only to Eid al-Adha when one is stationed in Mina for the stoning ritual. This distinction highlights the jurisprudential nuance between the two Eids, where the physical constraint of Mina on the Day of Sacrifice takes precedence over the general obligation of communal prayer.
